title: Not one sparrow (Luke 12:1–12)
hookLine: five sparrows sold for two pennies, and none forgotten; your hairs are numbered

lines: A CROWD TREADING ON EACH OTHER.
cards: Luke says the crowd had grown past counting, so big that people were treading on one another. And Jesus turns first to his own friends and talks about fear.
Theirs: fear of being found out, fear of powerful people, fear of standing before judges one day and not knowing what to say. It's a heavy start.
Then, to make his point, he reaches for something small from the marketplace: sparrows, sold five at a time.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "Are not five sparrows sold for two farthings, and not one of them is forgotten before God?" Farthing is the King James word for a small coin; the Greek says assarion. Now set Luke beside Matthew.
In Matthew, two sparrows are sold for one farthing. In Luke, five for two.
Some readers do the arithmetic: pay for four, and the seller throws in a fifth for free, a bird not even worth a price. And not one of them, Jesus says, is forgotten before God.

teach.h: THE HAIRS OF YOUR HEAD, NUMBERED.
teach.b: Then he comes closer: "But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore: ye are of more value than many sparrows." Numbered.
Not loved in general, as a crowd, but known down to a detail you don't even know about yourself. That's the ground under everything else he says here. Don't fear those who can only kill the body.
Say openly who you belong to. And when you're dragged before authorities, don't rehearse a speech, because, as he puts it, "the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour what ye ought to say."
In Acts, Luke's second book, Peter and Paul do stand before councils and governors.
Courage, in this passage, doesn't come from being tough.

teach.h: NOT ONE OF THEM IS FORGOTTEN BEFORE GOD.
teach.b: It comes from being known: if not one sparrow is forgotten, Jesus tells his friends, they need not fear.

how: The hymn His Eye Is on the Sparrow draws on the sparrow sayings in Matthew and Luke, and Francis of Assisi is remembered for preaching to the birds.

games.q: you're at a market in Galilee. sparrows are two for one coin. you hand over two coins. how many birds do you get?
games.why: Matthew says two for a farthing; Luke says five for two. some readers say the fifth is thrown in free, and not one of them is forgotten before God.

practice: Think of the thing you're most afraid of this week, and hold it for a moment. Then picture the fifth sparrow, the one thrown in for free, and the line that not one of them is forgotten.
If you pray, place your fear next to that sparrow; if you don't, simply hold the fear and the sparrow side by side.
